Ukraine says the satellite communication system it uses for drone missions
has been placed under restrictions. Ukraine's military uses Star Shield.
The military version of Elon Musk's Starlink impures Greg Myry.
Ukraine's defense ministry said in a statement that "without warning,

Ukraine says that when its drones exceed 100 miles per hour, which they routinely do,

Ukraine says it's in contact with the U.S. government and SpaceX to try to sort out the problem.

The president has been telling Ukraine to stop attacking Russian oil facilities,

President Trump has wrapped up a midterm campaign rally in Montana.
That rally, his second of the day in Arizona, Trump defended the airplane he's using as Air Force
One, saying he accepted it from the Qatari royal family because you take gifts when they're given
to you. The Justice Department is escalating its threats to local election jurisdictions
as a midterms approach. NPR's Miles Parks reports that the DOJ sent a list of
alleged non-citizen voters to L.A. County this week.
The county clerk for L.A., Dean Logan, said the DOJ reached out to his office on Tuesday,
three weeks before Election Day, with a letter and a USB drive that allegedly included the names of
non-citizens on the county's voter rolls. In the letter, the department asked Los Angeles
to segregate vote-by-mail ballots returned by the people listed until their citizenship is confirmed.
Logan says he has not accessed the drive because he couldn't verify it was secure.
But if his office doesn't implement the process requested by the DOJ within 48 hours,
the department says it will sue to compel him to. That may not be successful. Judges have dismissed
dozens of other DOJ lawsuits during Trump's second term related to oversight of local election
processes. Miles Parks, NPR News, Washington. The Faculty Senate at Cornell University met
Wednesday begin a no-confidence process on university leadership over the handling of an allegation of
campus sexual assault in 2024. NPR's Alyssa Netw or any reports. University President Michael
Kotlikoff joined the faculty meeting to take questions and talk about what the school is
doing to address safety on campus. But faculty still went ahead on beginning a no-confidence
vote, which is expected in a few weeks. It's an opportunity to voice their dissatisfaction with
the administration. But ultimately, Kotlikoff's job will be in the hands of the board of trustees,
a group that includes donors and alumni. They'll be meeting on campus starting Thursday.
Alyssa Networney, NPR News, Ithaca, New York. This is NPR.
Now to Oregon, which has paused permitting for new data centers,
joining two other states with similar data center moratoriums. Oregon Public Broadcasting's April
Ehrlich reports that the move comes as data centers are proving to be a major issue in the
state's governor's race. Oregon's Democratic Governor Tina Kotlik directed the state's
environmental regulators to stop permitting new or expanding data centers until July.
The directive comes amid an unusually tight race for governor between Kotlik and a Republican
candidate, state Senator Christine Drazen. Oregon hasn't elected a Republican governor since the
1980s. Each candidate has accused each other of not doing enough to regulate Oregon's growing
data center market. Amazon is a big player here. Its executives quickly criticized Kotlik's directive
as abrupt, saying it will help billions of dollars in planned investment. New York and Texas have
similar permitting moratoriums. For NPR News, I'm April Ehrlich in Portland, Oregon.
